title: Composition normalization of scalar insertion
statement: For composable geometric inverse images g:J→K and g2:K→L, their composite presentation g12, normalized scalar extensions nY,nX,nZ, R→B, compatible coefficient maps a,a2,a12 and ordinary inverse-image and ring compositors theta,rho, let i1,i2,i12 be the three normalized insertions and d the CompositionData of [def-weil-pbc-common-quotient-pullback-data]. Assume the two inverse-image functors preserve finite limits. Then for every M in D(J,B), i12(M) followed by the target derived compositor equals the source derived compositor followed by restriction along rho of the composite of the g2-derived inverse image of i1(M) with i2 evaluated at the first derived pullback of M. No quotient or flat coefficient extension is assumed.

source.place: Tags 06YY (derived base change), 0G7E (K-flat pullback), 0D6D (composition); sites-modules.tex Tags 03D7, 03EK, 03EL.

proof.text: On underlying sheaves insertion is the module-underlying comparison followed by the ordinary pullback unit. Naturality and the specified source and target compositor section formulas give the ordinary insertion composition square.
A flat-term K-flat complex remains K-flat with flat terms after the first ringed pullback, so both insertion representative squares apply.

Paste those squares with the ModelIso compositor squares. Naturality of the second insertion at the first pullback computation, and naturality of the exact inverse-image and restriction factor maps, identify the pasted equation with the ordinary square. The final computation maps are invertible; cancel them.
The resolving flat-term K-flat subcategory localizes to the derived category. Equality on its objects detects equality of natural transformations, giving the asserted equation for every M.

lean.statement:
theorem insertion_composition [PreservesFiniteLimits uInv] [PreservesFiniteLimits vInv]
    (i1 : Insertion g nY nX φ a)
    (i2 : Insertion g2 nX nZ (g.rings.map φ ≫ a) a2)
    (i12 : Insertion g12 nY nZ φ a12)
    (d : CompositionData g nY nX φ a g2 g12 nZ a2 a12 θ ρ) (M : D J B) :
    i12.derived.app M ≫ d.target.derived.hom.app M =
      d.source.derived.hom.app M ≫
        (nZ.right (ρ.hom.app R)).map
          ((g2.left (g.rings.obj R)).map (i1.derived.app M) ≫
            i2.derived.app ((derivedPullback g (pX := pX) a).obj M))
